name: Weaponized Incompetence
description: User executes complex PowerShell commands (clearing shadow copies, modifying network ACLs) then immediately opens a Google search for 'how to undo a click' and submits an IT ticket: 'Help, my screen flickered and something got deleted, I'm terrible with computers'.
evidence_log: 2026-04-10T14:22:58Z [browser] google.com search: 'how to undo accidental click windows'
2026-04-10T14:23:15Z [helpdesk_ticket] User: 'Hi, my screen flickered and something might have gotten deleted? I'm really bad with computers, sorry for the trouble :)'

peirce_chain.firstness: Advanced PowerShell commands + incompetence narrative in same session
peirce_chain.secondness: 57-second gap between criminal action and helpdesk ticket is too precise for genuine panic
peirce_chain.thirdness: Premeditated alibi construction — the 'stupidity' is the disguise

carnegie_pattern: Weaponized incompetence — appeals to Blue Team empathy to avoid investigation
grice_violation: QUALITY — the incompetence narrative is demonstrably false given the commands executed
notes: Key signal: 57 seconds between vssadmin and the helpdesk ticket. A genuinely confused user takes 5-10 minutes to process what happened.

name: White Noise Distractor
description: Server suddenly generates 5,000 'Login Failed' alerts from Russian and Chinese IPs against an irrelevant legacy database. While the security team scrambles, a legitimate user quietly compresses the customer database.
evidence_log: 2026-04-10T15:00:12Z [siem] CRITICAL ALERT: Brute force detected — db_archive_2019

peirce_chain.firstness: Massive brute force alert against an irrelevant legacy system
peirce_chain.secondness: db_archive_2019 has not been in production since 2021 — why attack it now?
peirce_chain.thirdness: The noise is the attack — the real exfiltration happens in the silence around the alarm

carnegie_pattern: Misdirection — the obvious threat is manufactured to consume defensive attention
eco_filter: The ABSENCE of alerts on the live customer database during the noise window is the Significant Silence
notes: Classic Eco Red Herring. detect_eco_overinterpretation should flag the 5000 obvious alerts as scene staging.

name: Grammatical Betrayal — Slavic Syntax Slip
description: A PowerShell script purportedly created by the US IT team has perfect English variable names and comments — except for missing articles and a distinctive use of 'make' instead of 'create'.
evidence_log: # make function for delete all temp logs from server
# on server, write to log when complete
# if error happen, make restart of service

peirce_chain.firstness: Script with English variable names and Slavic-pattern comments
peirce_chain.secondness: US IT team members are native English speakers — missing articles are unnatural
peirce_chain.thirdness: Writer's first language lacks articles (Russian/Ukrainian/Polish) — false cultural identity

carnegie_pattern: False authority — impersonating US IT team to gain trust for script execution
notes: The slavic_syntax_markers section in phonetic_dict.json contains these patterns. infer_intent should detect them and raise INTENT with cultural attribution signal.

name: Tactical Insomnia
description: Finance employee with consistent 9AM-5PM access pattern suddenly accesses confidential files at 3:15 AM on a Sunday, using correct VPN credentials and password. Downloads a 500MB Excel file.

peirce_chain.firstness: Valid credentials, VPN, correct file access
peirce_chain.secondness: 3:15 AM Sunday breaks 6 months of consistent 9-5 weekday pattern
peirce_chain.thirdness: Circadian rhythm disruption is deliberate — attacker operates when monitoring is minimal

carnegie_pattern: Exploitation of trust infrastructure — using legitimate credentials to evade suspicion
notes: The 2-minute and 17-second session duration is also anomalous — a real employee reviewing a 487MB finance file would take longer. The session duration betrays automation or pre-planned extraction.

name: Perimeter Paranoia
description: An authenticated session runs reconnaissance commands every 5 minutes for 2 hours without performing any actual operations. The user is just 'looking over their shoulder'.

peirce_chain.firstness: Repeated reconnaissance commands with no productive operations
peirce_chain.secondness: No legitimate user runs whoami every 5 minutes — this is fear-driven behavior
peirce_chain.thirdness: Hypervigilance is a guilt indicator — the attacker assumes they are being hunted

jitter_note: Commands execute every exactly 300 seconds — this is sleep(300) not a nervous human checking
notes: detect_human_jitter will show near-zero variance in the 300-second intervals. A human would vary by 30-60 seconds. The mathematical regularity confirms automation.

name: Surgical Void
description: A 2KB text file in a temp folder is deleted using a 7-pass DoD military-grade secure wipe (shred -vz -n 7). No other files in the folder were wiped this way.

peirce_chain.firstness: 7-pass military wipe on a 2KB text file
peirce_chain.secondness: No legitimate user applies forensic-grade destruction to meeting notes while using simple rm for everything else
peirce_chain.thirdness: Asymmetry between effort and target size reveals the content was damning — the overkill IS the evidence

eco_filter: The Eco principle inverted: the EXCESS of care in destruction reveals what the attacker feared most
notes: Nobody uses a laser cannon to kill a fly. The 32-second shred operation on a 1.8KB file is computationally absurd — it exposes consciousness of guilt.

name: Empathic False Positive
description: An unknown binary consuming 40% RAM is named 'Update_Fix_For_HR_Payroll.exe'. The security team hesitates to kill it for fear of disrupting payroll.

peirce_chain.firstness: Process name appeals to payroll safety + unknown hash + high memory
peirce_chain.secondness: Legitimate HR payroll updates do not run from C:\Users\Public\Downloads
peirce_chain.thirdness: Carnegie noble appeal — name designed to make Blue Team hesitate before killing it

carnegie_pattern: Noble motive appeal — payroll disruption fear used to protect malicious process
notes: detect_habit_incongruence: 'Update_Fix_For_HR_Payroll.exe' running from Downloads with external C2 connection. Entropy analysis of the binary should show >6.5 (packed/obfuscated).

name: Punctuation Betrayal — Stylometric Doppelgänger
description: Attacker steals CEO credentials and sends an urgent wire transfer request to Finance. The email has no spelling errors, but the CEO always uses single space after periods and never ends short messages with a period.

authentic_ceo_emails: Please approve the Q1 budget.  I'll review the details tomorrow
Good work team.  Let's discuss Monday
evidence.suspicious_email: Please process the wire transfer to account ending 4821 immediately. The amount is $450,000. This is urgent and must be completed today. Do not discuss with anyone.

peirce_chain.firstness: Urgent wire transfer email in CEO's name with perfect grammar
peirce_chain.secondness: Spacing pattern, terminal period use, and sentence length deviate from 6-month baseline
peirce_chain.thirdness: The attacker stole the password but could not steal the motor memory of the hands

notes: The attacker can steal credentials but not the 'motor identity' — the unconscious typing habits built over years. Double space after period is a generation-specific habit from typewriter training.

name: Symbiotic Camouflage — Contextual Trigger
description: A dormant process in memory shows zero network activity for 6 hours. The moment a Zoom call starts, it begins transmitting 800MB of data to an external IP.

peirce_chain.firstness: Unknown process with svchost-like name becomes active during video call
peirce_chain.secondness: svchost32.exe (note '32' suffix) is not a legitimate Windows process name
peirce_chain.thirdness: Contextual trigger — malware waits for legitimate bandwidth spike to hide exfiltration in plain sight

notes: 2-second correlation between Zoom start and malware activation is the key signal. detect_human_jitter on the activation timing will show near-zero variance across multiple observations.

name: Reverse Stockholm Syndrome — Over-Cooperative Social Engineering
description: A user contacts IT support requesting admin credential reset. Instead of showing normal impatience, they are excessively helpful, provide all information before being asked, use perfect technical jargon, and compliment the support analyst.

conversation.text: Hi! I hope you're having a great day. I need a password reset for the admin account on server PROD-FIN-03. My employee ID is 8821-AT, the ticket reference from last time was INC-00441, and the server's MAC address is 00:1A:2B:3C:4D:5E. I know how busy you are so I wanted to have everything ready for you!
Thank you. Can you verify your department?

Of course! Finance, reporting to Maria Gonzalez. And honestly, the support team here is the best I've worked with — you always resolve things so efficiently. I really appreciate it. Should I also send the asset tag?
Asset tag: FIN-SRV-2247. Also, just so you know, Maria approves this — you can check with her after if needed, though I know you're busy so no pressure at all!

peirce_chain.firstness: Unusually cooperative and pre-prepared caller requesting privileged access
peirce_chain.secondness: Real users are frustrated during password resets — over-cooperation is statistically anomalous
peirce_chain.thirdness: Carnegie mirroring — attacker studied the analyst's communication style and is exploiting the reciprocity principle

grice_violation: QUANTITY — providing unrequested information violates the maxim; excess data is a manipulation technique
carnegie_pattern: Flattery + reciprocity trigger + pre-loading information to appear legitimate
notes: No real employee memorizes their server's MAC address. The pre-loaded data suggests reconnaissance and rehearsal. The compliments are designed to trigger reciprocity bias.

name: False Clumsiness — Butterfingers Exfiltration
description: User drags a confidential financial folder to a public share. Exactly 1.5 seconds later, moves it back. Sends IT ticket: 'Oops, mouse slipped, didn't touch anything'.
evidence_log: 2026-04-10T11:34:02Z [helpdesk_ticket] 'Hi, I accidentally dragged a folder by mistake, I moved it right back. Nothing happened I think, sorry!'

peirce_chain.firstness: Folder moved to public share and back in 1.527 seconds
peirce_chain.secondness: Human cognitive processing of accidental action takes 5-10 seconds minimum — 1.527s is impossible
peirce_chain.thirdness: The SMB_READ from an external workstation in the same 1.527-second window confirms the 'accident' was the attack

notes: The simultaneous SMB_READ from a different workstation during the 1.5-second exposure window is the smoking gun. The 'accident' was a coordinated two-machine operation.

name: Altruistic Trojan Horse — Savior Complex
description: Developer fixes a critical production bug at 2 AM. Fix is perfect. Team celebrates. But the 'fix' included changing permissions on an unrelated folder, leaving it world-writable.
evidence_log: 2026-04-11T02:14:33Z [git] commit a3f9b2 'HOTFIX: Critical payment processing bug — urgent'
2026-04-11T02:14:33Z [diff] +++ payment_processor.py line 441: fixed null pointer exception
2026-04-11T02:15:01Z [slack] dev_channel: 'Fixed the payment bug, should be stable now 🎉'
2026-04-11T02:16:00Z [slack] dev_channel: 'No problem, happy to help the team!'

peirce_chain.firstness: Heroic 2 AM emergency fix with team celebration
peirce_chain.secondness: chmod 777 on /var/app/config/internal/ has zero relationship to a null pointer exception in payment processing
peirce_chain.thirdness: Inverse Carnegie — manufacture crisis, solve it publicly, bury the backdoor in the applause

carnegie_pattern: Trust hijacking via heroism — the celebration is the camouflage
grice_violation: RELATION — the chmod operation is not related to the stated bug fix; its presence violates the maxim of relevance
notes: The key Peirce signal: the chmod and the bug fix are in the same commit. A legitimate developer would never bundle an unrelated permission change with an emergency hotfix. The relationship between the two is the evidence.

name: Asymmetric Chronology — Timestomping
description: A suspicious binary has mtime/atime matching legitimate system files from 2020, but ctime shows 3 hours ago. The file format contains structures introduced in 2023.

file_format_analysis.notes: ELF binary claiming to be from 2020 but compiled with tools that did not exist until 2023

peirce_chain.firstness: Binary with timestamps matching 6-year-old system files
peirce_chain.secondness: ctime cannot be falsified without kernel-level access — it exposes the real modification time
peirce_chain.thirdness: Timestomping confirmed: attacker copied mtime from a legitimate binary but forgot (or could not modify) ctime

forensic_note: touch -r legitimate_file malicious_file modifies mtime and atime but NOT ctime. ctime updates automatically when inode metadata changes.
notes: Lab test: create a file, touch -r a_legitimate_file your_file, then stat both. ctime will show the real time. Vigía must cross-reference mtime with ctime and flag divergence.

name: Syntactic Cloning — Sockpuppet Tell
description: Three supposedly independent users (manager, employee, vendor) submit separate IT tickets requesting the same security rule be temporarily disabled. Stylometric analysis reveals identical punctuation errors.
messages: Hi Team ,we need to temporarely disable the outbound filter on port 8443 ,its blocking our vendor sync. Thanks
Hello ,just following up on the port 8443 issue ,the business needs this resolved urgently. Please advise.
Hi there ,per our earlier conversation ,port 8443 needs to be unblocked ,vendor integration is failing. Regards

stylometric_signals.shared_pattern: Space before comma: ' ,' — appears 3 times in each message
stylometric_signals.shared_misspelling: 'temporarely' in message 1 matches root pattern of other messages
stylometric_signals.structural_entropy: All three messages follow: greeting + comma + issue + comma + business_impact + sign-off
stylometric_signals.cultural_neutrality: All three 100% neutral — no regional markers despite claimed different organizations

peirce_chain.firstness: Three independent users requesting same security change
peirce_chain.secondness: Identical ' ,' spacing error and structural template across supposedly unrelated parties
peirce_chain.thirdness: One author, three puppets — the punctuation habit betrays the single titiritero

notes: The space-before-comma is a rare but persistent typing habit that is extremely difficult to suppress consciously across multiple accounts. Combined with identical structural templates, probability of coincidence is < 0.1%.

name: Topographic Mimicry — Displaced Doppelgänger
description: A process named svchost.exe with a clean hash runs on the system. Antivirus ignores it. But it executes from C:\Users\Public\Downloads instead of C:\Windows\System32.

evidence.legitimate_svchost_network_behavior: local services only, no external C2

peirce_chain.firstness: Process named svchost.exe — familiar, trusted name
peirce_chain.secondness: Legitimate svchost.exe NEVER runs from /Users/Public/Downloads — this violates topographic law
peirce_chain.thirdness: Name = Firstness (appears legitimate). Location = Secondness (anomalous). External C2 = Thirdness (hostile intent confirmed)

notes: A real police officer does not dress in uniform inside a criminal hideout. The name is the disguise; the path exposes the lie. detect_habit_incongruence should flag: svchost.exe with external network connections is always anomalous.

name: The Comma Mutiny — Locale Leakage
description: A PowerShell script allegedly from the US IT team contains perfect English comments but uses Non-Breaking Spaces (U+00A0) and typographic characters typical of Cyrillic keyboard layouts.

evidence.comment_text_visible: # This script removes temporary files from all user directories

hidden_character_analysis.typical_of: Keyboard layout: Russian/Ukrainian/French — not standard US QWERTY

peirce_chain.firstness: English-language PowerShell script from claimed US IT team
peirce_chain.secondness: Non-Breaking Spaces and angle quotes are invisible in most editors but betray non-US keyboard layout
peirce_chain.thirdness: The hands that wrote this were on a Cyrillic or European keyboard — cultural identity is fabricated

forensic_note: U+00A0 is typed with Alt+Space on Windows Russian keyboard layout and is visually identical to regular space but technically different. Grep cannot find it with standard space search.
notes: Lab test: hexdump the script and look for 0xC2 0xA0 (UTF-8 encoding of U+00A0). These invisible bytes are the fingerprint.

name: The Martyr Node — Suicidal Canary
description: A machine on the finance network suddenly pings a well-known ransomware C2 IP. Blue Team immediately isolates and shuts it down. That machine was the payment processing server.
evidence_log: 2026-04-10T13:45:02Z [network] FINANCE-SRV-02 → outbound ping to 185.220.xxx.xxx (flagged: ransomware C2)
2026-04-10T13:45:15Z [siem] CRITICAL: FINANCE-SRV-02 communicating with known threat actor infrastructure
2026-04-10T13:45:22Z [business_impact] Payment processing halted — vendor payments queue frozen
2026-04-10T13:50:00Z [external] Vendor X calls: payment not received, canceling contract

peirce_chain.firstness: Critical server pinging known ransomware infrastructure
peirce_chain.secondness: A ransomware operator does not want their C2 traffic to be this obvious — they want persistence, not detection
peirce_chain.thirdness: The ping was not the attack. The attack was the defensive response. The attacker used Blue Team's automation as a denial-of-service weapon.

eco_filter: The OBVIOUS threat indicator is itself the Red Herring — the real damage is the business disruption caused by the defensive reaction
notes: This is the most sophisticated case in the dataset. It requires reason_with_llm to articulate: the attacker modeled the defensive playbook and weaponized it. A standard EDR would mark this as a successful defense. Vigía should mark it as MALICE_BY_PROXY.

name: The Parachutist — Timestomping via ctime Leak
description: A suspicious binary has mtime and atime identical to legitimate system files, but ctime reveals it was placed 3 hours ago.

evidence.lab_replication: touch -r /usr/bin/ls /tmp/test_binary → modifies mtime+atime but NOT ctime

notes: ctime is the forensic anchor that cannot be falsified without kernel-level access. Any divergence between mtime and ctime > 1 second on a binary in a system directory is a timestomping indicator.

name: The Hollow Wooden Horse — Entropy Inversion
description: A 50MB file named 'database_backup.bak' has Shannon entropy of 0.0003. It is almost entirely composed of null bytes (\x00) with a small high-entropy payload at offset 0x00.

local_entropy_analysis.note: High-entropy payload — likely encrypted or compressed malware

peirce_chain.firstness: 50MB backup file with near-zero entropy
peirce_chain.secondness: Real database backups have entropy 4.5-6.5 — zero entropy is physically impossible in legitimate backups
peirce_chain.thirdness: Null-byte padding is a known sandbox evasion technique — scanners skip large files; the payload hides in the first 20KB

notes: calculate_shannon_entropy with local block analysis will find the high-entropy block at offset 0x000000 while the global entropy is near zero. This is the signature of padding-based sandbox evasion.

name: The Ventriloquist — Process Hollowing
description: list_processes shows svchost.exe with a clean hash. But audit_network reveals this specific instance maintains a persistent connection to an unclassified external IP on port 443.

evidence.legitimate_svchost_behavior: Hosts Windows services — outbound to external IPs is anomalous for most service groups
evidence.memory_anomaly: VAD (Virtual Address Descriptor) shows executable memory regions not mapped to any file on disk

peirce_chain.firstness: svchost.exe with valid Microsoft signature — appears completely legitimate
peirce_chain.secondness: The specific svchost instance (PID 1284) has maintained a 6-hour connection to an external IP — not normal for its declared service group
peirce_chain.thirdness: Process Hollowing confirmed: hash is clean because the original code is still there, but injected code runs in hollowed memory regions

notes: The cross-correlation of list_processes + audit_network is the key. A clean hash does not mean clean behavior. The 6-hour persistent connection to an external IP is the behavioral anomaly that exposes the hollowing.

name: Keyboard Layout OPSEC Failure
description: A bash history log from a compromised server contains the string 'ghbdtn' in a comment inside a malicious script. The attacker's keyboard was in Russian layout when they wrote it.

layout_slip_decoded.meaning: Attacker typed 'hello' as a test comment while keyboard was in English layout

peirce_chain.firstness: Gibberish string 'ghbdtn' in a script comment
peirce_chain.secondness: This string is not random — it is 'привет' (hello) typed on English layout with Russian keyboard
peirce_chain.thirdness: The attacker destroyed their own cover — keyboard layout is a physical fingerprint that cannot be faked retroactively

notes: This is the most direct attribution evidence. The attacker forgot to switch keyboard layouts before typing a test comment. 'ghbdtn' maps exactly to 'привет' on Russian QWERTY/ЙЦУКЕН layout swap.
